final_answer: ICE FLOATS ON WATER BECAUSE IT IS LESS DENSE. THIS OCCURS DUE TO THE UNIQUE MOLECULAR STRUCTURE OF WATER. WHEN WATER FREEZES, ITS MOLECULES FORM A HEXAGONAL LATTICE HELD TOGETHER BY HYDROGEN BONDS. THIS STRUCTURE CREATES MORE SPACING BETWEEN MOLECULES COMPARED TO LIQUID WATER, INCREASING THE VOLUME AND REDUCING THE DENSITY. AS A RESULT, ICE FLOATS ON TOP OF LIQUID WATER.
